movement_source: row 'Return on equity (ROE) - Cash basis', column 30 Jun 20 (FY20) -> column 30 Jun 21 (FY21)
headline: CBA's return on equity (cash basis, continuing operations) rose from 10.2% in FY20 to 11.5% in FY21, a +130 bpts (+1.3 ppt) improvement. The bank's own decomposition states the increase was "due to the impact of higher profit (approximately 200 basis points), partly offset by an increase in capital levels (approximately 70 basis points)". On the statutory basis, ROE rose from 10.4% to 11.8% (+140 bpts). The results presentation corroborates the cash ROE movement (10.2% to 11.5%, +130 bpts) and the cash NPAT growth (+19.8%).

drivers.narrative: Derived, not disclosed: prior-period ROE (10.2%) x earnings growth (19.8%) = +2.02 ppt at constant equity. The bank states cash NPAT from continuing operations increased $1,428m or 19.8% to $8,653m, driven by a 1.7% increase in operating income, a 3.3% increase in operating expenses and a $1,964m decrease in loan impairment expense (LIE fell from $2,518m to $554m, -78.0%). The bank's own decomposition attributes "higher profit (approximately 200 basis points)" to the ROE increase.

Derived, not disclosed: total delta (+1.3 ppt) minus earnings_effect (+2.02 ppt) = -0.72 ppt (equity growth and interaction term). The bank states the ROE increase was "partly offset by an increase in capital levels (approximately 70 basis points)". Average equity rose from $70,805m to $75,187m (+6.2%). The $6bn off-market share buy-back supports ROE through a lower share count, and the DRP was satisfied by on-market purchase of shares (not issuing new shares), limiting equity growth from the DRP.

disagreements.explanation: The FY21 profit announcement restated the FY20 comparative to conform to current-period presentation; the restated value (10.2%) wins per source hierarchy.

limitations: The earnings_effect and equity_effect are arithmetic derivations (not disclosed figures), though they align closely with the bank's own stated decomposition of "approximately 200 basis points" and "approximately 70 basis points".
No dedicated ROE walk/bridge chart exists in either document; the decomposition is stated in words on page 30 of the FY21 profit announcement.

The FY20 comparative values were restated in the FY21 document; the FY20 profit announcement shows slightly different values (ROE 10.3% vs 10.2%, average equity $70,852m vs $70,805m, cash NPAT $7,296m vs $7,225m).
The equity_effect is derived as the residual and includes the interaction term; its direction is supported by the average equity increase and the bank's stated "increase in capital levels" offset.
